programme.title: Maati Maangey Khoon
programme.desc: Hariya is clueless about his parents and discovers that his family was destroyed by Thakur Balram Singh. He vows to take revenge, especially after his friend, who is Balram's nephew, also opposes him.

programme.title: Alag
programme.desc: Tejas, an odd boy who grew up in a basement, is moved to a rehabilitation centre after his father's death. When he starts displaying psychic powers, a scientist abducts him for experimentation.

programme.title: Jagan
programme.desc: Jagan, an artist by profession, befriends two siblings on separate occasions and they both fall in love with him. He is forcibly married to the elder sister by goons, creating troubles in his life.

programme.title: Asmaan Se Ooncha
programme.desc: Inspector Malik transfers to Mumbai along with his family and sets out on a mission to catch King, an underworld leader. However, a shocking revelation changes the course of their lives.

programme.title: Mr. Natwarlal
programme.desc: When Natwar's elder brother is framed for bribery, he decides to avenge his brother's humiliation and thus poses as a crime lord.

programme.title: Saajan Ki Saheli
programme.desc: Kunti abandons her baby in order to lead a lavish life and marries a rich man. Years later, she realises that her husband is indulging in an affair and is shocked to find out the truth about the girl.

programme.title: Mera Faisla
programme.desc: Raj wishes to marry Rati but faces humiliation from her father due to the stigma associated with his lineage. Soon, he decides to join the police force to restore his family's honour.

programme.title: Baadshah
programme.desc: Raj, a small-time private detective who is desperate for a big break, gets drawn into a political conspiracy when he is hired to rescue a hostage.

programme.title: Taqdeer Ka Tamasha
programme.desc: An officer shares a strained relationship with his brother Satya, a criminal. When he tries to collect evidence against a goon, he meets his sibling. But they are not aware of the gangster's secrets.

programme.title: Anari Ishq
programme.desc: Rama, a simpleton, is appointed as the bodyguard of Rajnandini, a rich girl. She soon falls in love with him but her brothers' violent nature gets in the way of her uniting with Rama.

programme.title: Dharmyudh
programme.desc: A successful man tries to reconnect with his old teacher only to find out that she is in deep trouble. Upon learning this, he decides to do everything he can to save her.

programme.title: Blackmail
programme.desc: Dev discovers that his wife, Reena, has been cheating on him with Ranjit. To teach them a lesson, he decides to blackmail the cheating duo as part of his revenge.

programme.title: Ranbanka
programme.desc: Rahul, an ordinary engineer, comes to Mathura with his wife and son. However, when a gangster gets attracted to his wife and forces her to marry him, he tries to find a way to stop his advances.

programme.title: Kehte Hain Muzko Raaja
programme.desc: Action Movie.

programme.title: Farz

programme.title: Hiraasat

programme.title: Karishma Kudrat Ka
programme.desc: Widower Vijay lives in a village with his family. He unwittingly makes an enemy in Lala and a bandit, Bhagad, who conspire and throw him out of the village. But Vijay soon returns as a changed man.

programme.title: Bloody Mary
programme.desc: In an attempt to fulfill their dreams, three friends get entangled in trouble related to a director's death. Meanwhile, they confront an inspector while trying to save themselves.

programme.title: Face To Face
programme.desc: An inspector gets suspended for his irascible behaviour. The situation worsens when he gets framed for the murder of an ex-politician's son and must prove his innocence.

programme.title: Avinash
programme.desc: Avinash, a singer and a dealer of stolen goods, finds his life turned upside down when some goons break into his house and assault his fiancee.

programme.title: World's Most Unexplained
programme.desc: S1 E23 — Curse of EgyptDeath shall come on swift wings to him who disturbs the peace of the King," so the famous inscription goes. Is there truly a curse that haunts the original discoverers of Tutankhamun.

programme.title: World's Most Unexplained

programme.title: Discovered by Disaster
programme.desc: S1 E4 — Forgotten Cities and Lost SanctuariesExplore evidence that ties a meteor strike to a Biblical tale. Delve into a treasure-filled tunnel revealed by a sinkhole in Mexico.

programme.title: Walking Through History
programme.desc: S1 E4 — Battle in the GlensTony Robinson goes on a four-day trek through the Kintail region of the north-western Highlands, examining the story of the Jacobite uprisings of the early 1700s along the way. He starts by visiting Iron Age dwellings in Shiel Bridge, and heads to the rebuilt castle on Eilean Donan, the original of which was destroyed after invading Spanish troops landed there and were attacked by British warships. Tony ends in Glen Shiel, the site of a climactic battle in 1719 where royalist troops defeated the rebels.

programme.title: Walking Through History
programme.desc: S2 E1 — The Path to StonehengeTony Robinson embarks on a 45-mile walk across Wiltshire, from Avebury to Stonehenge, telling the story of the remarkable development that occurred in the latter days of the Neolithic era. His route over chalk downlands and Salisbury Plain takes him through one of the greatest concentrations of prehistoric sites in Europe.

Pixar animation, with the voices of Dave Foley, Kevin Spacey and Julia Louis-Dreyfus.

Animated drama, with the voices of Irene Bedard, Mel Gibson and Christian Bale.

Fantasy adventure based on the book by CS Lewis, with Tilda Swinton, Georgie Henley, Skandar Keynes, Anna Popplewell, William Moseley, James McAvoy and Jim Broadbent, and featuring the voice of Liam Neeson.

Disney animated fantasy based on Lewis Carroll's novel, with the voices of Kathryn Beaumont and Ed Wynn.

Family comedy, starring real-life father and daughter Miley and Billy Ray Cyrus, alongside Emily Osment, Jason Earles and Mitchel Musso.

Animated adventure, featuring the voices of Ryan Potter, Scott Adsit and Daniel Henney.

Remake of 1961 Disney comedy The Absent-Minded Professor, with Robin Williams, Marcia Gay Harden, Christopher McDonald and Wil Wheaton.

Comedy adventure, starring Melissa McCarthy, Jason Statham and Rose Byrne.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The London and South East chefs Adam Simmonds, Tom Sellers and Adam Byatt go head to head cooking their main courses. At the crucial half way stage the chefs must do all they can to score highly.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's dessert course time as the London and South East chefs compete for one of two places in the judges' chamber and the competition couldn't be tighter.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's a tightly fought battle today as the two remaining London and South East chefs cook all four of their dishes again for the judges Prue Leith, Oliver Peyton and Matthew Fort. They're joined by special guest judge, Joy Hunter.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Three of the Central region's top chefs, returning champion Aktar Islam, Daniel Clifford's protégé Mark Poynton and ambitious newcomer Jason Hodnett go into battle. They begin with their starter courses.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Returning champion Aktar Islam, Daniel Clifford's protégé Mark Poynton and ambitious newcomer Jason Hodnett fight it out for fish course glory. After plating up late last time will Aktar manage to be on time today?

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The Central region chefs Aktar Islam, Mark Poynton and Jason Hodnett go head to head cooking their main courses for the veteran judge. With Mark and Aktar fighting for the lead can Jason sneak under the radar to take them by surprise?

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's dessert day and the Central chefs Aktar Islam, Mark Poyton and Jason Hodnett are all striving for one of two spots in the regional final. Will Jason's elaborate chocolate medal dessert see him triumph or sent home empty handed?

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The two remaining Central region chefs cook all four courses again for the judges Prue Leith, Oliver Peyton and Matthew Fort. They're joined by special guest judge Max Hastings.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's the starter course and as the chefs arrive they discover there's added competition following the London and South East region's shock result. The judges are joined by D-Day veteran George Batts.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's the fish course and those chefs who didn't make it onto the shortlist with their starters are hoping to do better. The judges are joined by Ken Sturdy who landed on Sword Beach on D-Day and who helped judge the North West region.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's the half-way point in finals week and those chefs who have yet to get a dish onto the shortlist are feeling the heat. The judges are joined by Baroness Trumpington who worked as a cypher clerk at Bletchley Park from 1941 to 1946.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's the last chance for the chefs to get their dish in contention for the final banquet and those who've failed to finish in the top three so far are going all out. Joining the judges is Celia Sandys, Winston Churchill's granddaughter.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's the moment of truth as the victorious four must put their finest hours on a plate for those who served both on the front line and the home front, such as D-Day veterans Ken Sturdy and George Batts.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Three top chefs from Scotland are out to impress this week's veteran judge and be crowned Scottish champion. Adam Handling has already won a number of industry awards and is full of confidence. His starter sets out to take the diner on a tour of the UKs best producers. He's up against Michael Bremner, who is hoping to impress with contemporary ingredients including Birch sap and Douglas fir oil. Ally McGrath is celebrating his nation's finest produce and making his very own version of haggis.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Three newcomers to the competition create their fish dishes in a bid to be crowned Scottish champion. The standard is so high the veteran judge is moved to tears.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Ally McGrath has been keeping the veteran judge entertained with his very individual approach. Also, the highly competitive Adam Handling has been showcasing the finest produce grown and caught in and around the UK in his menu. Once again Michael Bremner is out to show how inventive he can be.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: One chef will go home and today the veteran judge finds himself with a difficult decision to make. Inventive Chef Michael Bremner is recreating the Scottish deserts of his childhood, Adam Handling is sticking with his trademark Asian flavours and Ally McGrath is tempering chocolate for the very first time.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Scotland's two highest scoring chefs are cooking for judges for the very first time. Both chefs have decided to make changes to some of their dishes, taking on board criticisms made during the week by the veteran judge.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Chef Josh Eggleton is back for a third time. Last year he made the national finals when his starter was shortlisted for the banquet, this year he intends to go one step further and cook at the banquet. One of his rivals last time, Jude Kereama is also back and out to do better than he did previously. The third competitor is newcomer Chris Wheeler who is originally from Swanage in Dorset.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: There are some exciting dishes on the menu as the three chefs from the South West tackle the fish course. Chef Josh Eggleton is hoping to impress with an original take on Bolognese, just one of six elements on his complex fish dish.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the main course and Chef Chris Wheeler is out to show just how theatrical he can be, his ideas are surprising everyone in the kitchen. No one knows quite what to expect and the veteran chef is hoping it tastes as good as it looks.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the dessert course and it is Josh Eggleton who has come up with the most ambitious dessert. He is creating his own self-serve ice cream made from vegetables, he is making everything from scratch including toppings and syrups.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the head to head and the South West region's two highest scoring chefs are cooking for judges Oliver Peyton, Prue Leith and Matthew Fort. They are joined by guest judge, journalist and restaurant critic, Grace Dent.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Two newcomers to the competition are challenging reigning North West champion Matt Worswick. Adam Reid is Head Chef for one of the UK's leading culinary talents, and Kim Woodward who made history when she was appointed Head Chef at the Savoy Grill.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the fish course and reigning North West champion Matt Worswick has reason to be confident. However, Kim's confident she has got one up on Matt by baking her own black bread unlike Matt who's taking a shortcut.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the main course of the North West Regional heat and the scores mean this is a crucial round. Matt Worswick may be the reigning champion but he is not yet assured of a place cooking for the judges and he is feeling the strain.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's the dessert course and the three North West competitors are getting creative, producing some of the most original and stunning desserts. All three chefs are working in a hot kitchen, the tension is palpable, and this time one chef will go home.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The two chefs are cooking for judges Matthew Fort, Prue Leith and Oliver Peyton, and guest judge Lady Claire MacDonald OBE. There are stand out dishes from both chefs making it a difficult contest to judge.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Three of the finest chefs from Wales are competing to be crowned champion. Two chefs are back for a second time: Phil Carmichael, from Cowbridge, South Wales, is Executive Chef at Berners Tavern in London and Adam Bannister, is chef and co-owner of Slice in his home city of Swansea. Adam was crowed Welsh champion last year so this year Phil is back with something to prove. He plans to go home raising the flag for Wales. The third chef is newcomer Andrew Birch, also from Swansea.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the fish course and newcomer Andrew Birch is confident, he is passionate about seafood. He is celebrating the cockle which is harvested near his home city of Swansea. Adam Bannister has created an alter ego, Captain Bannister for his modern take on the old boil in the bag fish dinners and Phil has chosen to revamp the classic prawn cocktail.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Phil Carmichael is serving up his version of an OBE, a refined take on onions, bacon and egg. Adam is planning to serve up Wild boar on a spit, while Andrew turns up the heat when he combines strong Japanese flavours with a traditional roast.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the dessert course and one chef will go home. Phil Carmichael is determined it won't be him but not everything is going to plan when he tackles his 'Cup of Tea for Ma'am'. One of the accompaniments to his earl grey panna cotta just won't work. He has to make a difficult decision.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the head to head. The two highest scoring chefs from Wales are cooking for judges Oliver Peyton, Prue Leith and Matthew Fort who are joined by guest judge, blogger and food writer Rosie Birkett.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Three newcomers are competing to become regional champion. Daniel Smith, a former head chef for the Roux brothers, now runs his own restaurant in his beloved home county of Norfolk. Andrew Scott's worked with the best in the business, and he's concentrating on telling powerful stories as well as delivering perfect flavours. Danny Gill is a former head chef at Daniel Clifford's two star restaurant Midsummer House.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the fish course and the chefs are using some of the UK's best seafood: lobster, salmon and Cornish crab. Danny Gill is a chef who likes to use the very latest equipment to create the most intense flavours. He's going to great lengths to maximise the taste of his cucumber consommé and it is causing a lot of interest in the kitchen.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Two chefs are cooking venison. Danny Gill is making a venison wellington, inspired by his Dad, a former RAF chef who has served up Wellington for royalty at many air force banquets. While Andrew Scott has sourced his venison from the Queen's Scottish estate, Balmoral.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: This week three chefs from the central region are fighting to be crowned champion. One competitor will go home, only the two highest scoring chefs will make it through to the judging chamber. Danny Gill is facing his toughest day yet, choosing to make a staggering eight elements for his imaginative dessert.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The Central region's two highest scoring chefs are cooking for judges Oliver Peyton, Prue Leith and Matthew Fort, for the very first time. Joining them in the chamber is guest judge Enam Ali MBE, a food entrepreneur who set up The British Curry Awards.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Three of the most exciting talents from London and the South East region are competing for a place in the National Finals. Head chef Mark Froydenlund runs Marcus Wareing's two star restaurant. Russell Bateman is head Chef at The Grove in Hertfordshire and Ronnie Murray who heads up the Hix Restaurant group.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the fish course and chef Russell Bateman is celebrating the diversity of his beloved home town of London - by combining lobster with jerk spices for an ambitious fish course with seven key elements. Ronnie Murray's taking a risk with an ingredient which is close to the veteran judge's heart...and is planning to serve it at three different temperatures warm, deep fried and frozen. And two Michelin starred Mark Froydenlund is planning a novel way to present his dish.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the fish course and chef Russell Bateman is celebrating the diversity of his beloved home town of London - by combining lobster with jerk spices for an ambitious fish course with seven key elements. Ronnie Murray's taking a risk with an ingredient which is close to the veteran judge's heart...and is planning to serve it at three different temperatures warm, deep fried and frozen. And two Michelin starred Mark Froydenlund is planning a novel way to present his dish.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's the all-important main course and returning contender Mark Froydenlund is banking on it being his strongest dish. Russell Bateman is creating a beef dish, and Ronnie Murray's mixing a crown of lamb with a curried filling.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's the dessert course and the final chance for three of London & South East's most competitive and talented chefs to get through to the judging chamber, today the veteran judge will send one chef home.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the head to head and the two highest scoring chefs from the London and South East region are cooking for judges Oliver Peyton, Prue Leith and Matthew Fort. Joining this week as guest judge is Kevin Gould, an award winning food writer.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Mini Patel is back for a second attempt at the north east regional title but he is competing against two young newcomers, Tommy Banks and Chris Archer. Last year, Mini went home after the dessert course, so he is hoping to keep better control of his nerves this year.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the fish course and two chefs, Tommy and Mini, have very similar ingredients - both are cooking mackerel. But Mini is trying an original beetroot sorbet while Tommy is using wild woodruff and oyster leaf from his own garden. Chris Archer has chosen the king of the sea, turbot, but there is controversy in the kitchen.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the main course of the north east region and overnight there has been a dramatic development. It is a tough and emotional day for the chefs as they react to the news but they battle on in a bid to present a perfect dish with venison and wagyu-angus beef - the meat of the day.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is a highly emotional day for one of the chefs as he prepares a dish which is inspired by and a tribute to his own great Briton, his late grandfather. But all is not going to plan and the chef ends up making one key element three times in a bid to achieve perfection.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The two chefs are cooking for judges Matthew Fort, Prue Leith and Oliver Peyton for the very first time. Joining them as guest judge is John Williams MBE, the executive head chef at The Ritz, the only hotel to hold a royal warrant for banqueting.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is Chris McGowan's third time however, he is facing tough competition from Mark Abbott, head chef at Daniel Clifford's 2 Michelin star restaurant, Midsummer House, and also from Eddie Attwell who has just completed a year as head chef at Ardtara Country House in Upperlands.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Mark Abbott is pushing himself again plating up a complex fish course of the very finest produce. He is calling it Shellsational but at the last minute he forgets a key element. Returning chef Chris McGowan is refining cod and chips and Eddie Attwell is getting classical with the king of the sea, turbot.The repartee is relentless as the chefs jostle for top place on the leader board. Once again there is plenty of emotion as the veteran chef delivers the scores.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the main course and returning Chef Chris McGowan is feeling confident but part of his dish involves making his own venison sausages to serve with a venison rack, and getting it all done in time is straining his emotions. Eddie Attwell is also serving the meat but with a traditional Northern Irish dish called Dock pudding. Mark Abbott is pushing himself again, he is using wagyu beef and serving it with tongue and corn cooked in a variety of ways.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E8 — Sweden v TunisiaSweden v Tunisia (Kick-off 3.00am). Semra Hunter presents coverage of the Group F match at Monterrey Stadium in Mexico. Sweden have a fairly disappointing record of qualifying for the World Cup in recent times, only appearing three times since they finished third at USA '94, and they had to rely on the UEFA play-offs to secure their spot this time around. For Tunisia this is their third consecutive appearance at a World Cup finals and their seventh overall, and they'll hope to take advantage of the new expanded format and qualify for the knockout stage for the first time. They came up short in Qatar four years ago despite claiming a credible 0-0 draw with Denmark and memorable 1-0 victory over France, with a 1-0 loss to Australia ultimately seeing the Socceroos finish above them in Group D as they progressed to the last 16 alongside eventual runners-up, Les Bleus. With analysis from Karen Carney and Jobi McAnuff, and commentary by Joe Speight and Lucy Ward.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E9 — Spain v Cape VerdeSpain v Cape Verde (Kick-off 5.00pm). Mark Pougatch presents coverage of the opening match in Group H, held at Atlanta Stadium in the USA. Spain won this tournament in 2010 and are among the favourites to do so once again, having won Euro 2024 and qualified from a group containing Türkiye, Georgia and Bulgaria with five wins, a draw and no defeats. They were also runners-up to Portugal in last year's UEFA Nations League, and their squad boasts the talents of the likes of Barcelona stars Pedri and Lamine Yamal, who is an injury doubt for the group stage, and Manchester City's 2024 Ballon d'or winner Rodri. Cape Verde are one of the tournament outsiders and it would be a major upset should they manage to get a result this evening, but they impressed in qualifying, topping a group that contained the likes of Cameroon, Libya and Angola. They have few players among their ranks who would be widely considered as household names, but are likely to look to captain and all-time leading goalscorer Ryan Mendes for inspiration. With analysis from Juan Mata, Emma Hayes and Ange Postecoglou, and commentary by Sam Matterface and Lee Dixon.

programme.title: FIFA WC2026: S. Arabia v Uruguay
programme.desc: S5 E10 — Saudi Arabia v UruguaySaudi Arabia v Uruguay (Kick-off 11.00pm). Laura Woods presents all the action from both teams' first match in Group H, held at Miami Stadium in the USA. The Saudis caused an upset against South American opposition in their opener four years ago in Qatar when they prevailed 2-1 against eventual champions Argentina, but defeats at the hands of Poland and Mexico ensured that 1994 remained the only time they had progressed beyond the group stage, when the tournament was also held in the USA. Uruguay lifted the trophy in 1930 and 1950, but their run of three consecutive appearances in the knockout stage came to an end in 2022, when they failed to make it out of a group containing Portugal, South Korea and Ghana. The sides also met in the group stage of the 2018 tournament, when a goal by Luis Suarez gave the Uruguayans a 1-0 win. With analysis from Duncan Ferguson, Karen Carney and Jobi McAnuff, and commentary by Joe Speight and Lucy Ward.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E11 — Argentina v AlgeriaArgentina v Algeria (Kick-off 2.00am). Laura Woods presents coverage of the Group J match at Kansas City Stadium in the USA, as the reigning champions play their first game in defence of their title. The South Americans beat France on penalties in the 2022 final after the game had ended 3-3 after extra-time in one of the most thrilling finals of all time, with France's Kylian Mbappe scoring only the second ever hat-trick in a World Cup final. That was Argentina's third success at this tournament after victories in 1978 and 1986. They will be looking to become just the third country to retain the trophy and the first to do it since Brazil won back-to-back titles in 1958 and 1962. Their opponents today are playing in their first World Cup since 2014, when they made it through to the last 16 before losing to eventual winners Germany 2-1 after extra-time. That was the African country's best performance at this tournament after failing to make it out of the group stage in their other two appearances at the finals. With analysis from Patrick Vieira, Karen Carney and Duncan Ferguson, and commentary by Seb Hutchinson and Andros Townsend.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E9 — Spain v Cape VerdeSpain v Cape Verde (Kick-off 5.00pm). Mark Pougatch presents coverage of the opening match in Group H, held at Atlanta Stadium in the USA. Spain won this tournament in 2010 and are among the favourites to do so once again, having won Euro 2024 and qualified from a group containing Türkiye, Georgia and Bulgaria with five wins, a draw and no defeats. They were also runners-up to Portugal in last year's UEFA Nations League, and their squad boasts the talents of the likes of Barcelona stars Pedri and Lamine Yamal, who is an injury doubt for the group stage, and Manchester City's 2024 Ballon d'or winner Rodri. Cape Verde are one of the tournament outsiders and it would be a major upset should they manage to get a result this evening, but they impressed in qualifying, topping a group that contained the likes of Cameroon, Libya and Angola. They have few players among their ranks who would be widely considered as household names, but are likely to look to captain and all-time leading goalscorer Ryan Mendes for inspiration. With analysis from Juan Mata, Emma Hayes and Ange Postecoglou, and commentary by Sam Matterface and Lee Dixon.

programme.title: FIFA WC2026: S. Arabia v Uruguay
programme.desc: S5 E10 — Saudi Arabia v UruguaySaudi Arabia v Uruguay (Kick-off 11.00pm). Laura Woods presents all the action from both teams' first match in Group H, held at Miami Stadium in the USA. The Saudis caused an upset against South American opposition in their opener four years ago in Qatar when they prevailed 2-1 against eventual champions Argentina, but defeats at the hands of Poland and Mexico ensured that 1994 remained the only time they had progressed beyond the group stage, when the tournament was also held in the USA. Uruguay lifted the trophy in 1930 and 1950, but their run of three consecutive appearances in the knockout stage came to an end in 2022, when they failed to make it out of a group containing Portugal, South Korea and Ghana. The sides also met in the group stage of the 2018 tournament, when a goal by Luis Suarez gave the Uruguayans a 1-0 win. With analysis from Duncan Ferguson, Karen Carney and Jobi McAnuff, and commentary by Joe Speight and Lucy Ward.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E11 — Argentina v AlgeriaArgentina v Algeria (Kick-off 2.00am). Laura Woods presents coverage of the Group J match at Kansas City Stadium in the USA, as the reigning champions play their first game in defence of their title. The South Americans beat France on penalties in the 2022 final after the game had ended 3-3 after extra-time in one of the most thrilling finals of all time, with France's Kylian Mbappe scoring only the second ever hat-trick in a World Cup final. That was Argentina's third success at this tournament after victories in 1978 and 1986. They will be looking to become just the third country to retain the trophy and the first to do it since Brazil won back-to-back titles in 1958 and 1962. Their opponents today are playing in their first World Cup since 2014, when they made it through to the last 16 before losing to eventual winners Germany 2-1 after extra-time. That was the African country's best performance at this tournament after failing to make it out of the group stage in their other two appearances at the finals. With analysis from Patrick Vieira, Karen Carney and Duncan Ferguson, and commentary by Seb Hutchinson and Andros Townsend.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E8 — Sweden v TunisiaSweden v Tunisia (Kick-off 3.00am). Semra Hunter presents coverage of the Group F match at Monterrey Stadium in Mexico. Sweden have a fairly disappointing record of qualifying for the World Cup in recent times, only appearing three times since they finished third at USA '94, and they had to rely on the UEFA play-offs to secure their spot this time around. For Tunisia this is their third consecutive appearance at a World Cup finals and their seventh overall, and they'll hope to take advantage of the new expanded format and qualify for the knockout stage for the first time. They came up short in Qatar four years ago despite claiming a credible 0-0 draw with Denmark and memorable 1-0 victory over France, with a 1-0 loss to Australia ultimately seeing the Socceroos finish above them in Group D as they progressed to the last 16 alongside eventual runners-up, Les Bleus. With analysis from Karen Carney and Jobi McAnuff, and commentary by Joe Speight and Lucy Ward.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E11 — Argentina v AlgeriaArgentina v Algeria (Kick-off 2.00am). Laura Woods presents coverage of the Group J match at Kansas City Stadium in the USA, as the reigning champions play their first game in defence of their title. The South Americans beat France on penalties in the 2022 final after the game had ended 3-3 after extra-time in one of the most thrilling finals of all time, with France's Kylian Mbappe scoring only the second ever hat-trick in a World Cup final. That was Argentina's third success at this tournament after victories in 1978 and 1986. They will be looking to become just the third country to retain the trophy and the first to do it since Brazil won back-to-back titles in 1958 and 1962. Their opponents today are playing in their first World Cup since 2014, when they made it through to the last 16 before losing to eventual winners Germany 2-1 after extra-time. That was the African country's best performance at this tournament after failing to make it out of the group stage in their other two appearances at the finals. With analysis from Patrick Vieira, Karen Carney and Duncan Ferguson, and commentary by Seb Hutchinson and Andros Townsend.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E8 — Sweden v TunisiaSweden v Tunisia (Kick-off 3.00am). Semra Hunter presents coverage of the Group F match at Monterrey Stadium in Mexico. Sweden have a fairly disappointing record of qualifying for the World Cup in recent times, only appearing three times since they finished third at USA '94, and they had to rely on the UEFA play-offs to secure their spot this time around. For Tunisia this is their third consecutive appearance at a World Cup finals and their seventh overall, and they'll hope to take advantage of the new expanded format and qualify for the knockout stage for the first time. They came up short in Qatar four years ago despite claiming a credible 0-0 draw with Denmark and memorable 1-0 victory over France, with a 1-0 loss to Australia ultimately seeing the Socceroos finish above them in Group D as they progressed to the last 16 alongside eventual runners-up, Les Bleus. With analysis from Karen Carney and Jobi McAnuff, and commentary by Joe Speight and Lucy Ward.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E9 — Spain v Cape VerdeSpain v Cape Verde (Kick-off 5.00pm). Mark Pougatch presents coverage of the opening match in Group H, held at Atlanta Stadium in the USA. Spain won this tournament in 2010 and are among the favourites to do so once again, having won Euro 2024 and qualified from a group containing Türkiye, Georgia and Bulgaria with five wins, a draw and no defeats. They were also runners-up to Portugal in last year's UEFA Nations League, and their squad boasts the talents of the likes of Barcelona stars Pedri and Lamine Yamal, who is an injury doubt for the group stage, and Manchester City's 2024 Ballon d'or winner Rodri. Cape Verde are one of the tournament outsiders and it would be a major upset should they manage to get a result this evening, but they impressed in qualifying, topping a group that contained the likes of Cameroon, Libya and Angola. They have few players among their ranks who would be widely considered as household names, but are likely to look to captain and all-time leading goalscorer Ryan Mendes for inspiration. With analysis from Juan Mata, Emma Hayes and Ange Postecoglou, and commentary by Sam Matterface and Lee Dixon.

programme.title: FIFA WC2026: S. Arabia v Uruguay
programme.desc: S5 E10 — Saudi Arabia v UruguaySaudi Arabia v Uruguay (Kick-off 11.00pm). Laura Woods presents all the action from both teams' first match in Group H, held at Miami Stadium in the USA. The Saudis caused an upset against South American opposition in their opener four years ago in Qatar when they prevailed 2-1 against eventual champions Argentina, but defeats at the hands of Poland and Mexico ensured that 1994 remained the only time they had progressed beyond the group stage, when the tournament was also held in the USA. Uruguay lifted the trophy in 1930 and 1950, but their run of three consecutive appearances in the knockout stage came to an end in 2022, when they failed to make it out of a group containing Portugal, South Korea and Ghana. The sides also met in the group stage of the 2018 tournament, when a goal by Luis Suarez gave the Uruguayans a 1-0 win. With analysis from Duncan Ferguson, Karen Carney and Jobi McAnuff, and commentary by Joe Speight and Lucy Ward.

For Tunisia this is their third consecutive appearance at a World Cup finals and their seventh overall, and they'll hope to take advantage of the new expanded format and qualify for the knockout stage for the first time. They came up short in Qatar four years ago despite claiming a credible 0-0 draw with Denmark and memorable 1-0 victory over France, with a 1-0 loss to Australia ultimately seeing the Socceroos finish above them in Group D as they progressed to the last 16 alongside eventual runners-up, Les Bleus. With analysis from Karen Carney and Jobi McAnuff, and commentary by Joe Speight and Lucy Ward.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E9 — Spain v Cape VerdeSpain v Cape Verde (Kick-off 5.00pm). Mark Pougatch presents coverage of the opening match in Group H, held at Atlanta Stadium in the USA. Spain won this tournament in 2010 and are among the favourites to do so once again, having won Euro 2024 and qualified from a group containing Türkiye, Georgia and Bulgaria with five wins, a draw and no defeats. They were also runners-up to Portugal in last year's UEFA Nations League, and their squad boasts the talents of the likes of Barcelona stars Pedri and Lamine Yamal, who is an injury doubt for the group stage, and Manchester City's 2024 Ballon d'or winner Rodri. Cape Verde are one of the tournament outsiders and it would be a major upset should they manage to get a result this evening, but they impressed in qualifying, topping a group that contained the likes of Cameroon, Libya and Angola. They have few players among their ranks who would be widely considered as household names, but are likely to look to captain and all-time leading goalscorer Ryan Mendes for inspiration. With analysis from Juan Mata, Emma Hayes and Ange Postecoglou, and commentary by Sam Matterface and Lee Dixon.

programme.title: FIFA WC2026: S. Arabia v Uruguay
programme.desc: S5 E10 — Saudi Arabia v UruguaySaudi Arabia v Uruguay (Kick-off 11.00pm). Laura Woods presents all the action from both teams' first match in Group H, held at Miami Stadium in the USA. The Saudis caused an upset against South American opposition in their opener four years ago in Qatar when they prevailed 2-1 against eventual champions Argentina, but defeats at the hands of Poland and Mexico ensured that 1994 remained the only time they had progressed beyond the group stage, when the tournament was also held in the USA. Uruguay lifted the trophy in 1930 and 1950, but their run of three consecutive appearances in the knockout stage came to an end in 2022, when they failed to make it out of a group containing Portugal, South Korea and Ghana. The sides also met in the group stage of the 2018 tournament, when a goal by Luis Suarez gave the Uruguayans a 1-0 win. With analysis from Duncan Ferguson, Karen Carney and Jobi McAnuff, and commentary by Joe Speight and Lucy Ward.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E11 — Argentina v AlgeriaArgentina v Algeria (Kick-off 2.00am). Laura Woods presents coverage of the Group J match at Kansas City Stadium in the USA, as the reigning champions play their first game in defence of their title. The South Americans beat France on penalties in the 2022 final after the game had ended 3-3 after extra-time in one of the most thrilling finals of all time, with France's Kylian Mbappe scoring only the second ever hat-trick in a World Cup final. That was Argentina's third success at this tournament after victories in 1978 and 1986. They will be looking to become just the third country to retain the trophy and the first to do it since Brazil won back-to-back titles in 1958 and 1962. Their opponents today are playing in their first World Cup since 2014, when they made it through to the last 16 before losing to eventual winners Germany 2-1 after extra-time. That was the African country's best performance at this tournament after failing to make it out of the group stage in their other two appearances at the finals. With analysis from Patrick Vieira, Karen Carney and Duncan Ferguson, and commentary by Seb Hutchinson and Andros Townsend.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E11 — Argentina v AlgeriaArgentina v Algeria (Kick-off 2.00am). Laura Woods presents coverage of the Group J match at Kansas City Stadium in the USA, as the reigning champions play their first game in defence of their title. The South Americans beat France on penalties in the 2022 final after the game had ended 3-3 after extra-time in one of the most thrilling finals of all time, with France's Kylian Mbappe scoring only the second ever hat-trick in a World Cup final. That was Argentina's third success at this tournament after victories in 1978 and 1986. They will be looking to become just the third country to retain the trophy and the first to do it since Brazil won back-to-back titles in 1958 and 1962. Their opponents today are playing in their first World Cup since 2014, when they made it through to the last 16 before losing to eventual winners Germany 2-1 after extra-time. That was the African country's best performance at this tournament after failing to make it out of the group stage in their other two appearances at the finals. With analysis from Patrick Vieira, Karen Carney and Duncan Ferguson, and commentary by Seb Hutchinson and Andros Townsend.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Sweden v Tunisia (Kick-off 3.00am). Semra Hunter presents coverage of the Group F match at Monterrey Stadium in Mexico. Sweden have a fairly disappointing record of qualifying for the World Cup in recent times, only appearing three times since they finished third at USA '94, and they had to rely on the UEFA play-offs to secure their spot this time around. For Tunisia this is their third consecutive appearance at a World Cup finals and their seventh overall, and they'll hope to take advantage of the new expanded format and qualify for the knockout stage for the first time. They came up short in Qatar four years ago despite claiming a credible 0-0 draw with Denmark and memorable 1-0 victory over France, with a 1-0 loss to Australia ultimately seeing the Socceroos finish above them in Group D as they progressed to the last 16 alongside eventual runners-up, Les Bleus. With analysis from Karen Carney and Jobi McAnuff, and commentary by Joe Speight and Lucy Ward

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Spain v Cape Verde (Kick-off 5.00pm). Mark Pougatch presents coverage of the opening match in Group H, held at Atlanta Stadium in the USA. Spain won this tournament in 2010 and are among the favourites to do so once again, having won Euro 2024 and qualified from a group containing Türkiye, Georgia and Bulgaria with five wins, a draw and no defeats. They were also runners-up to Portugal in last year's UEFA Nations League, and their squad boasts the talents of the likes of Barcelona stars Pedri and Lamine Yamal, who is an injury doubt for the group stage, and Manchester City's 2024 Ballon d'or winner Rodri. Cape Verde are one of the tournament outsiders and it would be a major upset should they manage to get a result this evening, but they impressed in qualifying, topping a group that contained the likes of Cameroon, Libya and Angola. They have few players among their ranks who would be widely considered as household names, but are likely to look to captain and all-time leading goalscorer Ryan Mendes for inspiration. With analysis from Juan Mata, Emma Hayes and Ange Postecoglou, and commentary by Sam Matterface and Lee Dixon

programme.desc: Saudi Arabia v Uruguay (Kick-off 11.00pm). Laura Woods presents all the action from both teams' first match in Group H, held at Miami Stadium in the USA. The Saudis caused an upset against South American opposition in their opener four years ago in Qatar when they prevailed 2-1 against eventual champions Argentina, but defeats at the hands of Poland and Mexico ensured that 1994 remained the only time they had progressed beyond the group stage, when the tournament was also held in the USA. Uruguay lifted the trophy in 1930 and 1950, but their run of three consecutive appearances in the knockout stage came to an end in 2022, when they failed to make it out of a group containing Portugal, South Korea and Ghana. The sides also met in the group stage of the 2018 tournament, when a goal by Luis Suarez gave the Uruguayans a 1-0 win. With analysis from Duncan Ferguson, Karen Carney and Jobi McAnuff, and commentary by Joe Speight and Lucy Ward

programme.desc: S5 E9 — Spain v Cape VerdeSpain v Cape Verde (Kick-off 5.00pm). Mark Pougatch presents coverage of the opening match in Group H, held at Atlanta Stadium in the USA. Spain won this tournament in 2010 and are among the favourites to do so once again, having won Euro 2024 and qualified from a group containing Türkiye, Georgia and Bulgaria with five wins, a draw and no defeats. With analysis from Juan Mata, Emma Hayes and Ange Postecoglou, and commentary by Sam Matterface and Lee Dixon.

programme.title: FIFA WC2026: S. Arabia v Uruguay
programme.desc: S5 E10 — Saudi Arabia v UruguaySaudi Arabia v Uruguay (Kick-off 11.00pm). Laura Woods presents all the action from both teams' first match in Group H, held at Miami Stadium in the USA. The Saudis caused an upset against South American opposition in their opener four years ago in Qatar when they prevailed 2-1 against eventual champions Argentina, but defeats at the hands of Poland and Mexico ensured that 1994 remained the only time they had progressed beyond the group stage, when the tournament was also held in the USA. Uruguay lifted the trophy in 1930 and 1950, but their run of three consecutive appearances in the knockout stage came to an end in 2022, when they failed to make it out of a group containing Portugal, South Korea and Ghana. The sides also met in the group stage of the 2018 tournament, when a goal by Luis Suarez gave the Uruguayans a 1-0 win. With analysis from Duncan Ferguson, Karen Carney and Jobi McAnuff, and commentary by Joe Speight and Lucy Ward.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E11 — Argentina v AlgeriaArgentina v Algeria (Kick-off 2.00am). Laura Woods presents coverage of the Group J match at Kansas City Stadium in the USA, as the reigning champions play their first game in defence of their title. The South Americans beat France on penalties in the 2022 final after the game had ended 3-3 after extra-time in one of the most thrilling finals of all time, with France's Kylian Mbappe scoring only the second ever hat-trick in a World Cup final. That was Argentina's third success at this tournament after victories in 1978 and 1986. They will be looking to become just the third country to retain the trophy and the first to do it since Brazil won back-to-back titles in 1958 and 1962. Their opponents today are playing in their first World Cup since 2014, when they made it through to the last 16 before losing to eventual winners Germany 2-1 after extra-time. That was the African country's best performance at this tournament after failing to make it out of the group stage in their other two appearances at the finals. With analysis from Patrick Vieira, Karen Carney and Duncan Ferguson, and commentary by Seb Hutchinson and Andros Townsend.

programme.title: FIFA WC2026: S. Arabia v Uruguay
programme.desc: S5 E10 — Saudi Arabia v UruguaySaudi Arabia v Uruguay (Kick-off 11.00pm). Laura Woods presents all the action from both teams' first match in Group H, held at Miami Stadium in the USA. The Saudis caused an upset against South American opposition in their opener four years ago in Qatar when they prevailed 2-1 against eventual champions Argentina, but defeats at the hands of Poland and Mexico ensured that 1994 remained the only time they had progressed beyond the group stage, when the tournament was also held in the USA. Uruguay lifted the trophy in 1930 and 1950, but their run of three consecutive appearances in the knockout stage came to an end in 2022, when they failed to make it out of a group containing Portugal, South Korea and Ghana. The sides also met in the group stage of the 2018 tournament, when a goal by Luis Suarez gave the Uruguayans a 1-0 win. With analysis from Duncan Ferguson, Karen Carney and Jobi McAnuff, and commentary by Joe Speight and Lucy Ward.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E11 — Argentina v AlgeriaArgentina v Algeria (Kick-off 2.00am). Laura Woods presents coverage of the Group J match at Kansas City Stadium in the USA, as the reigning champions play their first game in defence of their title. The South Americans beat France on penalties in the 2022 final after the game had ended 3-3 after extra-time in one of the most thrilling finals of all time, with France's Kylian Mbappe scoring only the second ever hat-trick in a World Cup final. That was Argentina's third success at this tournament after victories in 1978 and 1986. They will be looking to become just the third country to retain the trophy and the first to do it since Brazil won back-to-back titles in 1958 and 1962. Their opponents today are playing in their first World Cup since 2014, when they made it through to the last 16 before losing to eventual winners Germany 2-1 after extra-time. That was the African country's best performance at this tournament after failing to make it out of the group stage in their other two appearances at the finals. With analysis from Patrick Vieira, Karen Carney and Duncan Ferguson, and commentary by Seb Hutchinson and Andros Townsend.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E8 — Sweden v TunisiaSweden v Tunisia (Kick-off 3.00am). Semra Hunter presents coverage of the Group F match at Monterrey Stadium in Mexico. Sweden have a fairly disappointing record of qualifying for the World Cup in recent times, only appearing three times since they finished third at USA '94, and they had to rely on the UEFA play-offs to secure their spot this time around. For Tunisia this is their third consecutive appearance at a World Cup finals and their seventh overall, and they'll hope to take advantage of the new expanded format and qualify for the knockout stage for the first time. They came up short in Qatar four years ago despite claiming a credible 0-0 draw with Denmark and memorable 1-0 victory over France, with a 1-0 loss to Australia ultimately seeing the Socceroos finish above them in Group D as they progressed to the last 16 alongside eventual runners-up, Les Bleus. With analysis from Karen Carney and Jobi McAnuff, and commentary by Joe Speight and Lucy Ward.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E9 — Spain v Cape VerdeSpain v Cape Verde (Kick-off 5.00pm). Mark Pougatch presents coverage of the opening match in Group H, held at Atlanta Stadium in the USA. Spain won this tournament in 2010 and are among the favourites to do so once again, having won Euro 2024 and qualified from a group containing Türkiye, Georgia and Bulgaria with five wins, a draw and no defeats. They were also runners-up to Portugal in last year's UEFA Nations League, and their squad boasts the talents of the likes of Barcelona stars Pedri and Lamine Yamal, who is an injury doubt for the group stage, and Manchester City's 2024 Ballon d'or winner Rodri. Cape Verde are one of the tournament outsiders and it would be a major upset should they manage to get a result this evening, but they impressed in qualifying, topping a group that contained the likes of Cameroon, Libya and Angola. They have few players among their ranks who would be widely considered as household names, but are likely to look to captain and all-time leading goalscorer Ryan Mendes for inspiration. With analysis from Juan Mata, Emma Hayes and Ange Postecoglou, and commentary by Sam Matterface and Lee Dixon.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E11 — Argentina v AlgeriaArgentina v Algeria (Kick-off 2.00am). Laura Woods presents coverage of the Group J match at Kansas City Stadium in the USA, as the reigning champions play their first game in defence of their title. The South Americans beat France on penalties in the 2022 final after the game had ended 3-3 after extra-time in one of the most thrilling finals of all time, with France's Kylian Mbappe scoring only the second ever hat-trick in a World Cup final. That was Argentina's third success at this tournament after victories in 1978 and 1986. They will be looking to become just the third country to retain the trophy and the first to do it since Brazil won back-to-back titles in 1958 and 1962. Their opponents today are playing in their first World Cup since 2014, when they made it through to the last 16 before losing to eventual winners Germany 2-1 after extra-time. That was the African country's best performance at this tournament after failing to make it out of the group stage in their other two appearances at the finals. With analysis from Patrick Vieira, Karen Carney and Duncan Ferguson, and commentary by Seb Hutchinson and Andros Townsend.

programme.title: Tyler Boeh: Wait for It

programme.title: Secret Nazi Expeditions

programme.title: Secret Nazi Expeditions
programme.desc: E6Runes are the letters of an ancient Germanic writing system that harkens back to a mythological age filled with heroes, magic, and mystery.

programme.title: Secret Nazi Expeditions

programme.title: Greatest Escapes of WWII
programme.desc: E2An adrenaline-fuelled dash through nazi-occupied Europe known as ‘The Flight of the Crow’, a death-defying escape across the world’s most perilous mountain range, and the largest escape of world war two - by men who chose death over dishonour.

programme.title: The Abyss: Rise And Fall Of The Nazis
programme.desc: E1In the wake of the First World War, Adolf Hitler identifies Benito Mussolini as his model and has one ultimate goal: to gain power in Germany.

programme.title: The Abyss: Rise And Fall Of The Nazis
programme.desc: E2Hitler appears to be eliminated after his failed putsch in 1923. Discover how the Nazi movement used democracy's tolerance in Germany to achieve a comeback with agitation and violence.

programme.title: Combat Ships
programme.desc: E3Explore the design flaws and human errors that condemned great ships to a tragic end. In 1628 the warship Vasa sank on her maiden voyage. Together with Vasa curator Fred Hocker, solve the mystery of why this great ship sank.

programme.title: Combat Ships
programme.desc: E4Destroyers and Cruisers showcases ships that with their speed and firepower became the backbones of 20th century navies. We tell the incredible story of USS Laffey, the WW2 destroyer that would come to be known as ‘the ship that would not die’.

programme.title: History Of Weapons

programme.title: History Of Weapons
programme.desc: E2Examining how warfare entered a new dimension as attacks from the skies became possible with weapons from incendiary arrows to drones.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft

programme.title: Combat Trains
programme.desc: E1Nazi Germany boasted that its locomotives were faster and more innovative. This programme examines that claim by looking at these ‘flying trains’.

programme.title: Combat Trains

programme.title: The Abyss: Rise And Fall Of The Nazis

programme.title: The Abyss: Rise And Fall Of The Nazis
programme.desc: E4President Hindenburg suspends freedom of speech and Hitler comes to power in 1933. The first concentration camps for political opponents are set up.

programme.title: Combat Ships

programme.title: History Of Weapons

programme.title: The Abyss: Rise And Fall Of The Nazis
programme.desc: E5In 1934, Hitler's government is firmly in the saddle. Most Germans support Hitler's anti-Jewish policy and the regime's terror soon escalates.

programme.title: The Abyss: Rise And Fall Of The Nazis
programme.desc: E6At the end of 1939, the German Army invades Poland. Examine how Hitler succeeded in pushing through his rearmament and war plans relatively unhindered.
